headline: Iran Severs Hormuz, U.S. Strikes Back; Ukraine Sees Odesa Port Attacks
subheadline: IRGC Navy closes Strait of Hormuz after U.S. targets merchant vessel, prompting U.S. strikes on Iranian bases in Qatar, Bahrain, Jordan, and Kuwait.
lede: The Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps has shut the Strait of Hormuz, citing U.S. intervention after a merchant ship ignored warnings. In retaliation, U.S. forces launched strikes on Iranian targets across the region, hitting bases in Qatar, Bahrain, Jordan, and Kuwait. Meanwhile, Russian forces intensified air attacks on Odesa’s port infrastructure, while Ukrainian counterattacks targeted drone factories in Kiev.

sections.title: Odesa Port Under Russian Air Assault
sections.body: Russian forces fired eight rockets, including six Х-59 and two Х-31П, at Odesa and Chornomorsk, targeting port infrastructure with Su-34, Su-30, and Su-57 aircraft. Ukrainian strikes hit the Aerodron plant in Kiev, destroying E-300 Enterprise drones, and damaged Fanplit's Fire Point-2 drone assembly. Russian troops have secured Bachevsk in the Sumy region, with ongoing battles in Shostka and Ulanovo sectors. Russian attacks also damaged civilian infrastructure in Chernihiv, injuring one worker and damaging three private homes.

sections.title: Iran Closes Hormuz, U.S. Bases Hit
sections.body: The IRGC Navy announced the closure of the Strait of Hormuz until further notice after a U.S. vessel was targeted. U.S. forces responded with strikes on Iranian targets, striking the Al Udeid base in Qatar and the Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain, causing fires and smoke columns. Iranian missiles also destroyed the command-and-control center and MQ-9 drone sites at the Prince Hassan base in Jordan. Explosions were reported at Bandar Abbas, Sirik, Bushehr, Jask, Lengeh, and near the Bushehr nuclear power plant, while Khuzestan cities Hendijan, Mahshahr, and Abadan were struck by enemy projectiles.

sections.title: Intelligence Assessment
sections.body: The simultaneous escalation in the Gulf and the Black Sea indicates a multi-front state-on-state conflict, with Iran and the United States engaging in reciprocal strikes on strategic military and industrial targets. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz imposes a global energy chokehold, while Russian advances in Sumy and Kharkiv threaten Ukrainian logistical hubs. Diplomatic efforts in Rome and Beirut must succeed to prevent further regional spillover.
